currentContext.business: PVP Ventures is redeploying capital generated from monetisation of its legacy real-estate assets (residential development on its land parcel at Perambur, Chennai, executed with partners Brigade Enterprises Limited, Rainbow Foundations Limited and Casagrand Builders Private Limited) into building an integrated healthcare platform in India. During FY2025-26 it acquired majority stakes in diagnostics, oncology and specialty-care businesses and is pursuing a 'house of brands' strategy spanning specialty services, diagnostics, teleradiology and senior care, targeting predictable long-term annuity cash flows.

Real Estate: Residential development at Perambur, Chennai (with Brigade Enterprises Limited, Rainbow Foundations Limited, Casagrand Builders Private Limited)

risks.risk: Leadership and key-management turnover during the transformation year
risks.note: The Executive Director & CEO, Mr. Arjun Ananth, resigned effective 25 October 2025, and two other Board members (Mrs. P J Bhavani, non-executive director, and Mr. Gautam Shahi, independent director) also resigned before year-end, during the same year the Company was reshaping its portfolio and building a new healthcare platform.

risks.risk: Dependence on legacy real-estate monetisation to fund the healthcare pivot
risks.note: The Company states it is redeploying capital from monetisation of legacy assets, with discipline, into healthcare; continued funding of its healthcare foray is thus tied to cash generation from its legacy real-estate operations rather than from the healthcare businesses themselves.

risks.risk: Integration risk from multiple, near-simultaneous acquisitions
risks.note: The Company completed majority-stake acquisitions in three separate healthcare entities (Biohygea Global, Optimus Oncology and 7Med India) within the same financial year while also operating existing subsidiaries and step-down subsidiaries, creating execution risk in integrating a newly assembled multi-entity platform.

The Company describes itself as transforming from a diversified legacy business into an integrated healthcare platform across four new pillars (Cancer Care, Renal Care, Senior Care, Women's Health/Diagnostics) — a change in the nature of operations that carries execution and demand-realisation risk distinct from its historical business.

Safetrunk Services Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, was struck off from the Registrar of Companies' records with effect from 1 July 2025 during the year under review, reducing and reshaping the Company's subsidiary base.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Real-estate projects already signed with Brigade Enterprises Limited, Rainbow Foundations Limited and Casagrand Builders Private Limited on the Perambur, Chennai land parcel progressed as per expectations, with revenue expected to show a substantial increase as apartments come up for sale
- The diagnostics division contributed to consolidated revenue during the year
- India's healthcare sector is described as entering a new era in which institutions must build integrated ecosystems, personalise care, innovate continuously and improve outcomes at scale
- Residential development projects already signed with Brigade Enterprises Limited, Rainbow Foundations Limited and Casagrand Builders Private Limited for a portion of the Company's land parcel at Perambur, Chennai, progressing as per expectations

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Reshaping the portfolio, strengthening leadership and institutionalising governance to build an integrated healthcare enterprise
- Pursuing a 'house of brands' strategy to build a healthcare platform spanning specialty services, diagnostics, teleradiology and senior care
- Focusing on healthcare services going forward, relying on cash flows from real-estate operations to fund its foray into healthcare through acquisitions
- Investing in the full continuum of care and creating connected, patient-centred platforms in line with the evolution of India's healthcare sector
- Proposed corporate rebrand from PVP Ventures Limited to Evervie Health Limited to reflect the healthcare-platform identity, subject to shareholder approval

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Expansion during FY2025-26 was in two tracks. On the legacy real-estate side, the Company progressed residential development projects already signed with Brigade Enterprises Limited, Rainbow Foundations Limited and Casagrand Builders Private Limited on a portion of its land parcel at Perambur, Chennai, as per expectations, with revenue expected to rise substantially as apartments come up for sale. On the healthcare-platform side, the Company completed acquisitions of majority stakes in Biohygea Global Private Limited, Optimus Oncology Private Limited and 7Med India Private Limited during the year, building out a diagnostics/oncology/specialty-care platform alongside its existing subsidiaries (PVP Corporate Parks Private Limited, Humain Healthtech Private Limited, and step-down subsidiaries Noble Diagnostics Private Limited and Apta Medical Imaging Private Limited). Safetrunk Services Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, was struck off from the Registrar of Companies' records with effect from July 1, 2025, leaving the Company with five subsidiaries (two direct, two step-down, plus the newly acquired entities) as on March 31, 2026.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Platform design and ownership: builds and owns mission-critical healthcare assets that form the foundation of an integrated platform
- Partner-led expansion model: collaborates with best-in-class operators and experts to expand reach, capabilities and market penetration
- Disciplined capital allocation: deploys capital selectively to strengthen the platform, unlock adjacencies and generate long-term annuity cash flows, funded by monetisation of legacy real-estate assets
- Procurement leverage and portfolio synergies across the healthcare portfolio to reduce costs and drive cross-portfolio referrals
- Digital infrastructure: modern technology platforms and data backbone intended to drive efficiency and interoperability across the portfolio

- Dependence on legacy real-estate monetisation to fund the healthcare pivot — The Company states it is redeploying capital from monetisation of legacy assets, with discipline, into healthcare; continued funding of its healthcare foray is thus tied to cash generation from its legacy real-estate operations rather than from the healthcare businesses themselves.
- Integration risk from multiple, near-simultaneous acquisitions — The Company completed majority-stake acquisitions in three separate healthcare entities (Biohygea Global, Optimus Oncology and 7Med India) within the same financial year while also operating existing subsidiaries and step-down subsidiaries, creating execution risk in integrating a newly assembled multi-entity platform.
- Fundamental business-model transition risk — The Company describes itself as transforming from a diversified legacy business into an integrated healthcare platform across four new pillars (Cancer Care, Renal Care, Senior Care, Women's Health/Diagnostics) — a change in the nature of operations that carries execution and demand-realisation risk distinct from its historical business.
- Corporate structure instability among subsidiaries — Safetrunk Services Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, was struck off from the Registrar of Companies' records with effect from 1 July 2025 during the year under review, reducing and reshaping the Company's subsidiary base.
